utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first witness is a protected witness. Before he comes in, a very limited number of procedural matters; in fact, only a couple, I think. I trust the Chamber will have received from us the paper on the limits of examination-in-chief of certain witnesses. Obviously we will be grateful for resolution of that at an early date, but there's no witness for whom it becomes relevant before next Tuesday. Might we deal with that at the same time as we deal with the Status Conference next Tuesday? There's an application to add a witness in particular circumstances, and obviously resolution of that will assist us because arrangements have to be made for his attendance. We are planning on the Sarajevo witnesses, and the Chamber will understand that our planning is, of course, in part - quite a large part - dependent upon resolution of the 92 bis applications that have been made in respect of those witnesses. There was a 92 bis application a couple of weeks ago and another one served at the end of last week, and we'd be grateful for the earliest possible resolution of those applications. Those are the only matters I wish to raise. And may the screens be lowered for the witness to come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, before that, we have been handed the thesis of the witness Dr. Budding, which was admitted before the recess. It should have an exhibit number. It might as well have the next Prosecution number, I should think. The registrar tells me it was at the request of the Defence it was admitted, so it can have a Defence number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 168, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, before the witness comes in, we understand that there are some time constraints in respect of him; is that right, Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There certainly are. Can I explain them? If so, in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There is a file of exhibits for this witness. I don't know if it's possible to give a number to them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, we'll do that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Prosecution Exhibit 514.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The -- there are a couple of video clips produced as exhibits. The Sanction system, as the Chamber knows, regularly allows for the transcript to be displayed on the screen. I understand there's a technical difficulty, and when we play the video clips, I'll have to direct you on a couple of occasions to the printed transcript as one of the tabs of Exhibit 514.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There has been a translation. If you'd like to take a seat. Mr. Nice and also Mr. Milosevic, let me remind you that this witness has voice distortion and, therefore, care must be taken over the microphones. Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your full name Drazen Erdemovic, you a Bosnian Croat born in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it right that you were party to the takeover of Srebrenica in July of 1995? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following the takeover of Srebrenica, were you and others of the detachment of which you were a part involved in killing people at the Branjevo military farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were killed by you and those with whom you were associated on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: According to what I could judge, about 1.000 persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you engaged in those killings, so far as you could judge, who was giving the orders that the killings should take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I personally received orders from Brano Gojkovic, but a lieutenant colonel brought us to that farm, as far as I was able to see his rank, and he told Brano what we should do that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking up the management chain from the lieutenant colonel, so far as you could see, to whom was he answerable? To what body, unit, army, or so on?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He was answerable to the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of either the takeover of Srebrenica or, later, the killings, who was the most senior military person you ever saw in the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The most senior military person that I saw in that area was on the 11th of July when General Mladic came to the town of Srebrenica after it had been taken over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I go back and trace the history that led to your involvement in these events, just one last general question: The accused Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. has raised as a possibility that the French secret service were engaged in causing these deaths in Srebrenica. Did you see anything at all to suggest the involvement at the time of any foreign government, French or otherwise, in what was happening?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were not involved. At least, I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you charged in respect of the killings of which you have already told us, by this Tribunal, and did you plead guilty, were you sentenced to a term of imprisonment which you have now completed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The summary that the Chamber -- with the summary before the Chamber, I now start at the beginning. Paragraph 2. Mr. Erdemovic, did you join the JNA in 1990, leaving at the end of March 1992, serving in Croatia in the military police?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return to Tuzla in April 1992, being a member --

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- of the Tuzla Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those -- was the Territorial Defence unit deployed to regular ABiH units and did you serve in an ABiH mortar unit as a scout between July and October 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 4. From October 1992 to November 1993 did you serve in the HVO in Tuzla or the Tuzla area, and were you subsequently arrested by them for the assistance you were giving Serb civilians crossing from Tuzla into territory controlled by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were released following that arrest. Paragraph 6. Did you move to Republika Srpska in November 1993, getting to Bijeljina, and in Bijeljina did you become aware of paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What paramilitary units were you aware of?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that there were the Panthers, a unit called Crni, then Mauzer's Chetniks and quite a number of other units whose names I cannot recollect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In November 1993, did you cross to Serbia, going to Titov Vrbas, staying with a friend until early 1994?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time was there a problem for men with Bosnian identity papers in that they would be returned, if detected, to the custody of the VRS and forcibly mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you decide with your wife to return to Republika Srpska where you had a relation living?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the border between Serbia and Republika Srpska, were you ordered to report, being a Croat, to the police station at Foca, but when you got to Foca, were you then told to move to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Bijeljina were you now aware of the same paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those I mentioned a moment ago. There were the same units there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the Crni unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know his name, but I do know his surname because we had known each other before. His surname is Vasiljevic, and his nickname was Crni, and the unit was called by his nickname, Crni, meaning black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this unit consisted of men from which town?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Mostly refugees from the surrounding places around Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts had these men been trained?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know and on the basis of what I heard, the commander Crni went to attend training in Pancevo, as did several others from his unit. I know about him because I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Panthers were commanded by whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Ljubisa Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many men in this unit, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe around 100, 120, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you give a brief account of the uniforms worn by both the Crni and the Panther units, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The Crni members mostly wore black uniforms, black overalls, and they had black berets. And members of the Panthers wore the uniforms of the army of Republika Srpska. Some wore red berets, some black berets or green berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What view did you form as to of which corps or similar these units were a part?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were a part of the Bijeljina corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they based in the Bijeljina corps barracks and were they guarded by the military police of the Bijeljina corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they used on regular or special missions and by whom were they instructed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were used mostly for special cases or missions, and I assume that they received instructions from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 15, briefly. Were you aware of a visit by Arkan to Bijeljina? If so, when, to what purpose, and with what effect?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think this was in November that Arkan came to Bijeljina, and he held a meeting with the local Serbs who were holding positions in that town, and they intended to carry out an operation. But I only heard about this. I don't know for sure. Apparently Arkan requested a certain sum of money for him to carry out a certain assignment. However, this was refused, and it was never carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we move on, can I just go back to one other question about the two units, that is the Crni and the Panthers. You've given an account of your recollection of the uniforms. What, if any, insignia did they have consistent with their names or otherwise identifying the group of which they were members?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can remember for the Panthers. They wore on their left sleeve a Panther, the symbol of a Panther. So I knew they were members of that unit. As for Crni, I can't remember exactly what kind of insignia they had as this was a long time ago, and I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as to the men who trained these units, can you say anything about the uniform or insignia of those men?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain your question, because I don't understand which men you're referring to, the men that were carrying out the training, as you've said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, were you aware of who trained these men? If not, we'll move on; if you were, I'll ask the next question.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I said that I know only about Crni and certain members of his units who went for training to Pancevo, and if they were trained in Pancevo, then probably they were trained by officers of the army of Yugoslavia. Now, what kind of insignia exactly they wore, I don't know what uniforms they wore at the time. I do know that the army of Yugoslavia had dark green uniforms, a combination of dark and lighter green coloured uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's sufficient. We'll move on. Paragraph 16. Did you have any allegiance to any particular sect or the army of any particular sect?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Religion? No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Religion, yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, nevertheless, join up as a soldier? And explain why, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I joined a unit that later came to be known as the 10th Sabotage Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. unit or detachment, which consisted of eight to ten soldiers, most of whom were Croats. There was one Muslim and one Slovene. I joined that unit I think in April of 1994, and this unit belonged to the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you join or feel the need to join?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I went to the military department in Bijeljina, I said I was a Croat and that I wanted to join a unit, and they told me that it would be best for me to join a unit that had already been formed of several Croats and Muslims, and that is what I did. And I joined the army, because if I hadn't joined then, I would have been arrested and mobilised the next day. I had no rights. If you were not in the army, you didn't have any rights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those initial eight to ten soldiers in the group that -- or the unit that was subsequently named as the Sabotage Detachment initially housed at a house in Dvorovi in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commander was whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The commander at the time was Zoran Manojlovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom were you trained?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I was trained by a former officer of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what skills?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In sabotage skills; planting explosives, acting and use of explosives and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that the person who trained you was a former officer of the army. Do you know one way or another whether his position with that army was current or past?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Past. He simply came there. He was a civilian after that. He did not want to be in the army. He came at the request of Zoran Manojlovic to show us how to use explosives and to train us in some sabotage skills that we should be aware of. He left after that training. He was no longer in the army. He did not belong to a single unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the eight to ten men supplemented by others? If so, from where did those others come, and who became the commander of the unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the month of October, Lieutenant Milorad Pelemis came to our unit. He then became the commander of our unit. That is when our unit became bigger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the other recruits come from, if you can help us?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: From all parts of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In December 1994, did a number of the new recruits go for training? If so, how many roughly, and where?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that there were between 50 and -- between 40 and 50 persons who went for training to Pancevo, to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the military barracks there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When those who had gone returned, what did they bring with them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They brought some new weapons, explosives, a few uniforms; things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What if any authorisation would have been required for them to pass to and from Pancevo in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In order to enter Republika Srpska from Serbia, I think that no particular authorisation was needed. However, in order to leave Republika Srpska and go to Serbia, somebody would have to know about that in order for them to cross the border, because there were quite a few police forces on the border, at the border crossings between Bosnia and Serbia -- I mean, Republika Srpska and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the training in Serbia last?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Two to three weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those who had been trained, did they remain with the units up to and including the time of the takeover of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your time as a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, as it came to be called, and in March or April of 1995, did you meet three particular officers, one of whom had a nickname?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What uniforms did they have, and what did they say about where they'd come from and what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They had uniforms of the army of Yugoslavia. They were dark green, dark green and light green, a lighter shade of green. They said -- because I mean they were in an office and I was in that office too. They said that they had come from the army of Yugoslavia, that they were from Pancevo. They knew the persons from my unit who had been in Pancevo, and they also knew Commander Pelemis. One of these officers had a nickname; Jenki.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they do while they were stationed with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The first time I saw them, they were visiting the Main Staff. The second time, when they came again, they were conducting training with us from the 10th Sabotage Detachment. This training took place in Vlasenica where the Vlasenica platoon from my unit was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly what time was this training?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was also in March, beginning of April. I don't know, I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've spoken of the Vlasenica platoon. Was the detachment divided into two platoons, one from Vlasenica and one from Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These officers who were training the Vlasenica platoon, did they acknowledge openly coming from the VJ?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember now exactly whether they specifically acknowledged that, but according to what I heard, what was being said in that office, I came to the conclusion that that was the truth. And I know it's the truth, because when they came to Bijeljina to the barracks there, they once asked Pelemis to give them the special permits so that they could pass through the checkpoints where they were supposed to pass. And they also asked for a replacement of their licence plates on their vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they indeed provided with replacement licence plates so that they could pass less obviously coming from outside?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How well equipped were they with weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they had normal weapons with them that were used by officers mostly at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time, was your unit in receipt of uniforms and/or weapons? If so, who organised them and where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: For the most part, our uniforms and weapons were obtained by Pelemis through some channels that he had in Serbia. I don't know which channels these were but I know that this came from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Physically how were they brought to you from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Pelemis, if he would go there to Serbia, he would bring this in the car that he would take to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, weapons and uniforms. All of this would come from Serbia to Republika Srpska. Pelemis would make sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us some idea of the number of trips involving weapons that you were aware Pelemis made, or some idea of the quantity of weapons he brought with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The weapons that he brought with him were special weapons, for the most part, that they procured. I don't know where and how. The quantity was not big because there were a few, perhaps about ten of these special weapons only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us about - paragraph 24 - about the two platoons. The commander of the Bijeljina platoon was whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the Bijeljina platoon was Franc Kos. And the commander of the Vlasenica platoon was Lule. I only know his nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom was -- beg your pardon. The detachment was commanded by Pelemis. From whom did he receive orders, as you understood it?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Pelemis received orders from persons who were in the Main Staff in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. -- I'm sorry, I've started forgetting my own language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If and when you have trouble with your own language, just take time and, if necessary, I'll ask you the question again, and don't feel under any pressure. So the question is: Who instructed Pelemis? Can you put a name to the person who instructed him?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that. It was Colonel Salapura who instructed him. He was on the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anybody else on the Main Staff who you can remember giving instructions to Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I know definitely about Salapura. I don't really know about the others. There were others probably too, but I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the name of Pelemis's deputy, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Radoslav Kremenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the 10th Sabotage Detachment was deployed to an area of Republika Srpska under the command of another brigade, who retained command of the Sabotage Detachment unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question? I didn't quite understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the 10th Sabotage Detachment was deployed or used in areas of Republika Srpska under the command of another brigade, who actually controlled the Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It depends. If Pelemis would be there, then it would be Pelemis. And if Pelemis would not be there, then it would be the commander of that group, and he would always be -- he would always be in a position to command the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to July 1995, did the detachment take part in missions in the safe area of Srebrenica? If so, for what purpose?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They tried to liquidate Safet -- Naser, Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many such missions were there, roughly?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think two or three. I don't know exactly. I know of two, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you connect in your own mind the timing of the attack on Srebrenica to Oric's movements in some way?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I learned that afterwards, after the fall of Srebrenica, that Naser Oric was at a meeting in Tuzla with his non-commissioned officers and commissioned officers. I don't know whether this is 100 per cent true, but I heard -- that's what I heard, and I believe that that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I move to the attack on Srebrenica, just two matters of detail. You received wages -- this is paragraph 26. You received wages for your work in the Sabotage Detachment. Do you know who provided the money for those wages?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I received wages, and -- and as far as I know, everything came through Pelemis and persons who were in charge of logistics in our unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 31. In your operations in Republika Srpska, did you ever see VJ or SDB units active?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 33, coming to the attack on Srebrenica. On the 10th of July in the morning, did you receive orders that you were to go to Srebrenica? If so, where did the orders come from?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I personally was told this by Franc Kos, commander of the platoon. He said that we should go home and take our personal toiletries and clothes and that we should come back to barracks and go out on assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 514 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 514, tab 1. Sorry about the microphone. This is a map. It's not entirely clear on the screen because of its scale but the Chamber has it in tab 1 for hard copy reference purposes. It's Srebrenica at the bottom right-hand part of this map, Zvornik in the middle, and other places shown further up the map towards Bijeljina. I want you to deal with this fairly briefly, please, Mr. Erdemovic. Instructed in the way that you were, did you board a bus with others from your platoon, so instructed, head towards Bratunac where you arrived at about 2.00, and there did you join 25 to 30 members of the Vlasenica platoon?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What military police were present, if any?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were there because we came on the bus. The bus stopped in Bratunac, in front of the prefabricated buildings that were used by the military police of the army of Republika Srpska. I can say that this belonged to the Bratunac Brigade because they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later did you board trucks and go towards Skelani, passing a UN checkpoint on the way?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you reach the southern elevation above Srebrenica that evening and stay the night, and were you joined by Pelemis that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, did the assault on Srebrenica begin?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The town of Srebrenica itself. But before that, there had been fighting, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, were you told about the attitude you should take towards civilians in the course of the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the morning of the 11th, Pelemis told us that we should send civilians to the football stadium, that we should not shoot at civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Court is now viewing on the screen tab 2 of the exhibit which shows Srebrenica at the bottom. Was your unit divided into four groups? If so, led by whom? Can you give us the names of the leaders of the four groups?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Four groups were planned. One group was Marko Boskic, the other was Franc Kos, the other was Zoran Malic, and I can't remember exactly now whether it was Brano Gojkovic or Lule who led the remaining one. I can't remember that exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you joined by another group of about 15 men? If so, can you name the group from which they came?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They belonged to the Zvornik Brigade, as far as I know. It was the group of Drinski Vukovi, the Drina Wolves. Their commander was Legenda. Rather, "Legenda" was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Pelemis tell you whether other units were involved and give you any idea where they came from?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think -- I can't remember exactly. I think that he said they were units from Sejkovici, Vlasenica, Milici, Bratunac; all the surrounding villages around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commander of the Drina Wolves was who?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I just know his nickname. His nickname was Legenda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did it appear to you was in charge of the attack on Srebrenica generally?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The leader of that attack -- I mean, at first I thought it would be Pelemis who would be in charge of the attack. However, according to what I could see, it was Legenda who was the one who was in charge of this action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the participation of your unit in this attack something that was expected by you or was it unexpected and unusual?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can speak about the persons from the Bijeljina platoon. We had never taken part in such actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not going to deal with the geography leading to Srebrenica in detail. The witness can deal with that if it's relevant and if he's asked. I have an eye on the clock and wish to finish by half past ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 39. Did your group move from the south of the town towards the town itself? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Apologise. Being displayed at the moment is Exhibit 514, tab 3. The hard copy may merit your attention because there are a couple or three points marked on it, A, B, and C, which don't show up and the witness will deal with them briefly. Perhaps he can have a hard copy in front of him, or it could even go on the overhead projector. The points are not particularly critical although they are of interest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the attack start at about 10.00 and reach the centre of town by about noon?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that the attack was mounted at position B on tab 3, was the mosque still standing? Was it attacked? Did it have a flag? Was the flag removed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. That flag was not removed from that mosque. It was taken off the mosque that was to the south, at the very entrance into the outskirts of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm grateful to Mr. Waespi, who I should have reminded the Chamber is sitting with us today, for correcting me on that, my mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened at the mosque, if anything? At the other mosque.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see on this picture, this mosque which was in the centre of town is no longer there. That's what I can say. I cannot see anything else, so I can't say anything about the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come across a group of elderly civilians, about 200 in number?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. I think that when we talked about this the question was what I think, approximately how many civilians had been in Srebrenica from what I could see, and then I said that there were about 200 of them, perhaps, but for the most part, they were elderly persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what direction were they moving, if you saw them moving?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if somebody would go out of the house -- every person was asked to leave the house, actually, to get out of the house and to walk in front of the soldiers so they would not get killed. And that's what they did, they walked in front of us. We came from the southern side and they walked in front of us towards the centre of town, and then they went on further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in what direction that would have taken them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know then but I know now that Potocari was in that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly how many Serb soldiers were involved in the attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think there could have been about 500 to 700 soldiers. I think. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you encounter any resistance from Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: There wasn't any stronger resistance, only a few sniper shots. There wasn't any kind of fierce resistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any destruction of any houses or any single house even?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Detail, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we got down into town, we were told that as we walked ahead -- I mean, since there were shots coming from that hill above Srebrenica, it was a Praga, and it was used to remove any resistance coming from the other hills. And when it would be noticed from where a sniper shot had come, they would tell us to burn the first thing that would be near us so that we could in this way show how far we had advanced. And that's how this house was burned, because it was the first one there so that this person could show where he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any looting happen?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom and of what sort of property?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, afterwards when Srebrenica was taken, these local Serbs -- these local Serbs who for the most part had been born in Srebrenica and who had fled to Bratunac or Vlasenica or Zvornik, they took TV sets, video recorders, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before we move on to the detail of what happened in the course of the attack, can we look, please, at tab 4 of Exhibit 514. It's a video clip, and I think that the transcript won't be available, so the Chamber may want to cast its eyes over without dwelling at length on the transcript at tab 4 and I'll ask the witness a couple of questions about what we see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The transcript's available for review generally if we need to -- or in detail if we need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But help us, please, Mr. Erdemovic. That was a United Nations vehicle that was in a ditch. We saw a man with a United Nations helmet tucked into his belt carrying -- a United Nations cap tucked into his belt carrying a United Nations helmet, and we saw General Mladic. Do you know personally anything about this particular event or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is a UN vehicle. The soldier carrying the cap in his belt and holding a UN helmet in his hand is a person who belonged to my unit, and he was a driver. He was Commander Pelemis's driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else did you recognise on that video?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I recognised Mladic. I recognised Zivanovic, and I saw a person who was the communications man in my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly -- look very briefly at tab 5, please. Who do you recognise here, apart from Mladic who is in middle? Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes; Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And tab 6. Tab 6 has the man with the beret and the helmet.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You can't see him clearly here, but that is the person I referred to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have we on this clip, or on this still -- sorry, on the clip of the video or on the still, a picture of the normal uniform of people in your detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Namely who?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On this still we see the driver who was in our unit and who drove Commander Pelemis. His nickname was Cico.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And is the uniform he's wearing the uniform of your detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to tab 3, the hard copy that the Chamber may wish to look at, and to the events on the advance into Srebrenica. In the course of that advance, was there one man who was mistreated, in your judgement, by men from the group, and did Pelemis instruct what should happen to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: That person was mistreated. He was not mistreated by a single person from our unit, he was mistreated by people who had come down from the surrounding hills and who belonged, I don't know exactly to which, Vlasenica, Sehovici units, but Pelemis did order a soldier to kill him, a soldier from my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By reference to the photograph, aerial photograph tab 3, whereabouts did this killing happen and how was it done?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The killing happened here, and the person from my unit slit the throat of this man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your group told by Pelemis to report by radio when General Mladic and others reached town? Paragraph 46.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time did Mladic arrive? Did you notify Pelemis of this fact?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Pelemis was informed about it, and Mladic arrived in town shortly afterwards, maybe between 1.00 and 2.00 p.m., I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Mr. Waespi for helping me to make matters easier for the Chamber. Can we just look at tab 20 very briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man who slit the throat on the instructions of Pelemis, is he Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. shown in this picture?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's the man number 2, marked with a 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I return to the arrival of Mladic in town. Can we look, please, at tab 7, which is a -- there was a part of tab 7 which is the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours will see that tab 7 is an extended entry of a video clip of various things. We're just going to be looking at the very last part on what is page 9, at the bottom right. Page 8 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If you could just pause there for a second, please. The Chamber will have seen on the foot of page 8 of tab 7 congratulations being offered by Mladic, his saying the town is clean -- an unidentified voice saying the town is clean, you can drive by car with no problem. Then reference to Krstic, on to Potocari, Bratunac, don't stop at Potocari. I think that's the passage we were at although we weren't having either the transcript or the translation. Press on, please. We're now, I think, on the top of page 9.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Cameraman, cameraman. "Come on Krle, over here. "We brought in the flag two years ago to the day. Two years ago on the 11th of July. This is free. "General, sir. "That's good. Excellent. Forget about history, please. Go so we'll come out at Bratunac. Come on. Forget about history. Forward. "Here we are on the 11th of July, 1995, in Serbian Srebrenica. On the eve of one more great Serbian holiday we present this town to the Serbian people. After the rebellion against the Turkish governor, the moment has finally come for us to take revenge on the Turks here. "Look, everything over. Come on. Naser's hideout, brother. How did it get here?"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The end of that clip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this clip reflect the timing of the arrival of Mladic into Srebrenica, as you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we look at tab 8, which is a clip -- a still from that clip, do we see a flag lying on the wooden structure in the foreground?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What flag was that, and then can you tell us about any of the people shown on the picture?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It is the flag with a crescent and star. It was taken off the first mosque as we entered town. On this still, you can't see it clearly now, but there are several soldiers from my unit on that picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By name?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Velimir Popovic, Stanko Savanovic, and a person whose name I said before I didn't want to state and my position remains unchanged today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look again --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mike, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at clip -- tab 9 of the exhibit. The Chamber may remember this man is not very well shown on the still. Who is that in the foreground?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It is Zivanovic, General Zivanovic, who was commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 10, please. Can you tell us who is shown here?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph we can see the commander of my unit, Milorad Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he the one on the left or the right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He is on the right, the first on the right as I face the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now want to move to the period the 12th to the 15th of July. On the 12th of July, were you instructed that you would be leaving Srebrenica, but you went not to Bijeljina but to Vlasenica, and were you on the 13th of July informed that you had to attend a funeral in Trebinje some way away, reaching there on the 14th of July, and then moving back to Vlasenica on the morning of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 16th of July, did Brano Gojkovic inform you of new instructions?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you have to go and what were you told about your duties at this early stage?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano Gojkovic just said that Pelemis had said that we were going into action. Just then, he didn't explain anything in connection with that operation nor what our assignment would be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We left the house in which the Vlasenica platoon was housed, and we went in the direction of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 11, please, on the ELMO. What does this show?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We can see here the buildings and the quarters where we stopped with our vehicle. Brano Gojkovic and the driver, Aleksandar Cvetkovic, entered the reception area, and they came out shortly afterwards together with a lieutenant colonel and two military policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On their return to your vehicle, what did you do? Where did you all go?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When they returned, when they came out, this lieutenant colonel and two military policemen, they said that we should get into our vehicle and that we should follow the vehicle in which the lieutenant colonel and the two military policemen were. And their vehicle was an olive-green colour, and it had licence plates of the army of Republika Srpska, and the brand name was an Opel Kadet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went, as you were to discover, to this farm shown at tab 12 of Exhibit 514; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just go back briefly to tab 1, if we could do that. Can you tell us which figure on this marked map shows where the farm is?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So some considerable distance from Srebrenica from which, as we're going to discover, buses were coming. When you got to the farm, what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we reached the farm, there were several persons there in uniforms of the army of Republika Srpska, and then this lieutenant colonel ordered these people to leave the farm and said that only one guard should remain, who was a guard there anyway as far as I was able to see. And then Brano said what was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Explain, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano said that buses would start arriving with civilians from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you to do to the people coming from buses?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were to be executed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was with you on the detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Franc Kos, Marko Boskic, Goronja Zoran, Stanko Savanovic, Brano Gojkovic, Aleksandar Cvetkovic, Marko Boskic, and Golijan Zoran -- I'm sorry, Vlastimir Golijan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may have told us this: Was there anybody there with a military police sign on their sleeves; and if so, from what area did you calculate he came?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: There were those two military policemen who had come with that lieutenant colonel. As far as I was able to judge, they must have been military policemen from the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A brief description of the appearance of the lieutenant colonel, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He was tall, heavily built, about 1 metre 90 centimetres in height. He had prominent features and a loud voice. He had a receding hairline. His hair was not all grey, but it was greyish, turning grey, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and he was between 40 and 50 years of age, in my assessment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already told us at the beginning of your evidence that you took part in the executions. We'll come to a little of the detail in minute or so, but did the colonel stay, the lieutenant colonel stay while the executions were going on or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He did not; he left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having been given instructions, did you raise any objection to what you were being asked to do?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not just me, but two other persons from my unit raised the issue why this was being done. I personally couldn't understand why this was going on. I couldn't believe it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reaction to your objection? How was your objection overborne?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano Gojkovic said that, "You join them and line up and give them your rifle and see whether they will shoot at you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the event, what time, roughly, if you can remember, did the first bus arrive?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Around 10.00, between 10.00 and 11:00 in the morning. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What guard was there on the bus, if any?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the bus, as far as I was able to see, there were two military policemen. I don't know if they were there on each of the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the ground, armed and ready to execute people coming from the bus were a total of how many men?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Eight men with weapons. They were members of my unit. Later, members came from the Bratunac unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Starting at the beginning, were people ordered off or taken off the bus in groups of ten at a time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By reference to the photograph - and we can put a hard copy on the overhead projector to assist, perhaps - whereabouts were they shot?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were shot here in this field, just below the farm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the first ten had been shot, were another ten taken off or ordered off the bus and were they lined up and shot?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then so on progressively for that bus and for later buses that arrived at the farm; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Executions by your group, were they done in a sequential way, starting at one end of the field and moving towards the farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a time when a machine-gun was used but that was found to be not efficient because it left people mutilated who had to be finished off with pistols?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the first victims off the first bus blindfolded and with their hands tied but later did you find the people coming off without having their hands tied?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those men whose hands were not tied have to do something with their identification cards?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were ordered to take out everything they had in their pockets by way of documents and to throw them down in the corner of the garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly how many -- well, I'll come to the total number of buses in a minute. Was there any resistance by any individual of those executed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I just think that one person, when these people from Bratunac came, but only one person tried to resist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll deal with the arrival of the men from Bratunac. What time did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but maybe between 2.00 and 3.00. I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they take over the executions from you or did they kill alongside you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They took over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was their killing orderly, using the field in a sequential way, or was their killing all over the field?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They first mistreated several of those persons because they recognised them, and then they started killing them all over the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the one man who resisted was in the time that the people from -- the men from Bratunac were there and he was killed, I think; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 65. Was the one man who told you he'd helped Serbs get out of Srebrenica and provided a piece of paper with some relevant telephone numbers on it, and did you refer his case to Brano Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He told me this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Brano Gojkovic do with this man?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I tried to save that man, but Brano Gojkovic said that he didn't want to have any witnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the victims men?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that farm, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Their age range and the clothes they were wearing, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were wearing civilian clothes, and they were between maybe 18 and 60 years of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already given a total estimated number for those killed right at the beginning of your evidence. Were you given any information as to how their bodies were to be moved or buried?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This person who was the guard at the farm said that they would be buried, that pits would be dug and that they would be buried in this field below the garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time. I haven't finished in the first session. I've been one hour and 20 minutes. I think I probably can finish in other ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now. Mr. Erdemovic, would you remember not to speak to anybody during the adjournment about your evidence until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. If the registrar would come up, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the last bus had arrived and its occupants been executed, did you see the lieutenant colonel again?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What instructions did he give you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He gave instructions to Brano. He said that at that house in Pilica there were about 500 persons from Srebrenica and that they were trying to break down the door and get out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your reaction?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we said -- I said that I wouldn't do it any longer and that I couldn't do it any longer. I was supported in this by some persons from my unit, so we did not go to do that at the house in Pilica. However, persons from Bratunac went there and did it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to tab 1 of Exhibit 514. Is Pilica shown at the top close to where the farm is, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Letter A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's now move on to tab 15. Although you didn't go to do what the lieutenant colonel wanted you to do, did you go to the area and wait while the men from Bratunac did what was requested, or apparently did what was requested of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Brano said that the lieutenant colonel had said that we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. should go to the cafe, that it was in this place called Pilica. The cafe was opposite this cultural centre in the village of Pilica where these persons from Srebrenica were detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The cafe is on the left of tab 15. Pilica Dom is on the right of tab 15. We then have a front view of Pilica Dom on tab 16, and an aerial view of it looking over the cafe towards Pilica Dom on tab 17; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On arrival, did you see any bodies on the ground in front of Pilica Dom?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did see a few bodies lying in front of the Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your position on the other side of the road, what did you hear of what the men from Bratunac were apparently doing?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: While we were still at the farm when these people from Bratunac were there, automatic gunfire could be heard. And I also heard a few hand grenades explode. I could infer that these were explosions that were caused by hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Pilica itself while --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Pilica itself while these things were going on, how normal or abnormal was the life going on around the area? Were there people there in neighbouring properties? Just describe, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I think that these persons, the inhabitants of Pilica knew what was going on. On the basis of what I could see, there were people in the street, also in front of the Dom. There was a civilian police checkpoint. They could see all of it too. I think -- I did not notice anything out of the usual except for the persons who were killed on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us with the number of people who were killed at Pilica Dom that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I only heard what this lieutenant colonel had said, that there had been 500 persons. No, I don't know how many there actually were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when it was all over, did you hear anything said about people who survived?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when these people from Bratunac came back, this lieutenant colonel talked to them, and he also talked to some people from my unit, and he said if there were any survivors, there were. I heard the men from Bratunac then say that there was a female whose brother had been detained in that Dom and that she did not want to part with her brother and that therefore she was killed too. I don't know how true all of that is, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 13 of Exhibit 514. Does this show, as you understand it, women gathered at Potocari, the place in the direction of which you'd seen elderly people moving at your takeover or part in the takeover of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as this picture is concerned, I can say that yes, I assume that this is Potocari, but I did not see it myself, so I don't know exactly whether this is Potocari. I cannot know whether these are the civilians who I had seen. I see that there are civilians, and I assume that they are in Potocari. I can't say anything. I recognise one person that cannot be seen here, a person who is on the left-hand side. This person took part in the execution on the farm, and as far as I know, he was an inhabitant of Srebrenica before the war. I think that he was born in Srebrenica and that he had fled to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he one of the men who had come from Bratunac part way through the killing to take over from you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had he also been one of the men responding to the lieutenant colonel's instructions at Pilica Dom?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 79. Later in July or August of 1995, were you injured and did you land up going to the military hospital in Belgrade where you saw other members of the VRS from Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a nearby -- in a nearby bed was there man who explained he'd worked for the state security in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he didn't say it to me personally, but that is what he was saying, that he was a member of a unit that belonged to the state security of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything about involvement of the Serbian MUP in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He said that he had allegedly been in Srebrenica, that his unit had been in Srebrenica, that they took over Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his unit was a MUP unit from Serbia; is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was a member of a unit that belonged to the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a couple of sentences, the procedure whereby VRS soldiers such as yourself could land up being treated in Belgrade, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: According to what I know, I was wounded during the night - I don't know exactly - around the 20th of July. I was heavily wounded. The hospital in Bijeljina did not have the resources needed to help me. I was transferred to the military hospital in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we now please look at a short video clip of the ceremony, tab 19.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Radislav Krstic: "Soldiers of the Sabotage Detachment, Serbian heroes! Allow me to salute you myself in the name of the members of the Drina Corps as well as the name of the commander of the main staff and congratulate you on the day of the formation of the unit." Soldiers: "Thank you!" Radislav Krstic: "With your activities so far, you have demonstrated how a soldier of the army of Republika Srpska should fight. You have completed all of your tasks very successfully until now, without losses, which is a worthy achievement. We are in a situation --"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's all I require of this. The remainder of the transcript can be found at tab 19.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, was this a ceremony at which you were present?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened so far as you were concerned and indeed also the leader of your platoon?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I was not lined up at the time. I was sitting on the sidelines because I had been wounded. I couldn't stand on my feet. Then I was given the rank of reserve sergeant. Franc Kos, commander of the Bijeljina platoon, got the rank of reserve lieutenant, I think; second lieutenant, I think. I can't remember now. And this was the anniversary of the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've seen tab 20 before for the purposes of looking at figure number 2. Figure number 1 is whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It's Franc Kos, commanding officer of the Bijeljina platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was promoted as you've described. We look at number 2, the man who slit somebody's throat on instruction. What's his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: His name is Zoran. I don't know his surname, but his nickname is Malic, and he belonged to the Vlasenica platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two other documents, please, to look at. Tab 22, I think, or 21. 21. This document, please, that the Chamber has in English and we're looking at the original. Just explain what it is, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: This is a certificate allowing me to cross over to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in the period denoted by the 20th of February, 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see Mladic's signature at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next exhibit, please. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 22 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next exhibit, tab 22, is a contract on admission of persons to the army of Republika Srpska on a fixed-term contract. It sets out your name, your rank as sergeant, your duties, and again it is a document signed, as we can see at the end, by Mladic. The date it gives for the starting of your engagement is February 1995. That doesn't accord with your recollection. Can you explain why it only dates from February 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot explain because I did not receive any explanations then as to the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other signature at the foot of the document is, I think, Pelemis whom you've been referring to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Two other questions just to tidy up matters that I dealt with earlier. We saw a clip of a UN vehicle being hauled out or being prepared for being hauled out of the ditch by men of your detachment where Mladic was present. Do you know how many other, if any other, UN vehicles were seized by VRS soldiers in the course of the takeover of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there were any others or just do you not know?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't want to make any assumptions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Second question: You've described the special weapons that came with Pelemis by car from Serbia for your detachment. The first question of two: Can you identify the particular type of weapon that he was bringing in?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He was bringing in an Uzi. I think it is Israeli made. Then Hecklers, then a sniper, a SAR rifle that had been brought in earlier. Also, special arrows were used with infrared rays. Also some Russian weapons, small-calibre weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question: Did any of these -- my last question: Did any of these weapons have identifying serial numbers or other marks that would indicate where they'd come from or what force they'd originally belonged to?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think that all these weapons had their serial numbers and also the origin on them where they had been manufactured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not so much concerned with places of manufacture but whether they had identifying marks showing of what unit or army or whatever they'd originally been property, if any.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You'll be asked further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Erdemovic, in relation to these events that you are testifying about, if I understood you correctly, during the attack on Srebrenica, you were in Srebrenica all the time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was in Srebrenica from the 10th until the 12th in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That must be the time when the attack was actually taking place.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on, you were involved in these events that you yourself said were unbelievable, sometime from the 16th onwards; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, at the time of the attack or at the time when these events took place, the ones that you describe later, could you see or hear of the participation of anyone from Serbia in these events?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I could not see anyone who was from Serbia according to what I could see or tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, I understood from the examination-in-chief that for a while you were in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Alija Izetbegovic's army, before you joined the army of Republika Srpska, and then for a while you were in the HVO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which order did all of this take place? You were in the JNA while the JNA was still in existence?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you were -- you went on to the army of Alija Izetbegovic; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for a short time you were in the Croat army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you stopped being in the Croat army, and then you moved on to the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I must remind you to speak one at a time. Mr. Erdemovic, would you remember, keep an eye on his microphone and wait until it's turned off, and then reply. Yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, according to the information that I have, and a short while ago we saw a document here which shows that you came to the territory of Yugoslavia, and I noted it here as I was watching the screen, the document was issued on the 20th of February, 1996; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which date did you come across to the territory of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 20th -- my microphone doesn't work. So then when that document was issued to you, I saw that it says something like official trip there or something like that.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that same date you went to the territory of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was on that very day or perhaps a day later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, perhaps a day later. According to the information I have here, already after ten days or so you were arrested in the territory of Yugoslavia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I have a document here, an official document, which is entitled "Criminal report," and it says: "Against Erdemovic Drazen, father's name Viktor," born et cetera, et cetera, Donja Dragunja, village of Tuzla. Is that right? Those are your particulars?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ethnic Croat, married, father of one child, locksmith, unemployed, Radika Lakic [phoen] 144 is your address, detained from 1996, from the 3rd of March, 1996. So you were in detention as of the 3rd of March 1996; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says here from 2200 hours onwards.
